primitives.name: Mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium of the constant-sum PK game: indifference conditions and the zero-correlation prediction
primitives.verbatim_quote: This classical game-theoretic analysis has shown that a msNE exists in the PK-game. As such, classical game-theory predicts for the PK-game that there is no expected correlation, positive or negative, between location-conditional shot-volume and conversion-rate in the game’s equilibrium.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: p_t = probability the taker T shoots Center, dimensionless in [0,1]; q_G = probability the goalkeeper G stays Center, dimensionless in [0,1]; p_t*, q_G* = msNe mixing probabilities (both 1/4); pi_T = taker payoff = conversion rate, dimensionless probability; pi_G = goalkeeper payoff = non-conversion rate = 1 - pi_T (constant-sum, printed p.2-3); coefficients 0.7, 0.1, 0.3, 0.9 are cell conversion/non-conversion probabilities, dimensionless. Note: printed Eq. (3) OCR reads the leading coefficient as '7' (the dot of '.7' is lost in extraction); the stated solution p_t* = 1/4 and payoff pi_T* = 3/4 confirm 0.7. Existence rests on Nash (1950) via Kakutani (1941) fixed point (printed p.3).
primitives.assumptions: Discrete one-shot constant-sum two-player game; strategy sets restricted to {Center, Corner} for exposition (results claimed not unique to this restriction, printed p.2); payoffs ordinally consistent with the data; both players expected-payoff maximizers or minimax (same msNe under fixed sum, printed p.3); no pure-strategy Nash equilibrium exists (Table 1 best-response arrows, printed p.3).
primitives.breakdown_regime: The zero-correlation prediction holds only at equilibrium: any behavioral deviation (optics, risk aversion) or misspecified payoff cells breaks it. Repeated-play learning dynamics, asymmetric information about the goalkeeper's dive tendency, or non-constant-sum preferences (e.g., utility over manner of failure) exit the model's scope. The msNe equalizes expected returns definitionally (printed p.4), so observing unequal conditional returns is evidence against equilibrium play, not against the theorem.

layer2.mapping: NFL directional subgames (run left/right, pass left/right, kick direction) are constant-sum matching games between play-caller and defensive coordinator: the caller wants to avoid coordinating, the defense wants to coordinate. At msNe the defense is indifferent on the margin, so charted call-volume vs success-rate by direction should show zero correlation; a significantly negative subset correlation is the same behavioral-deviation signature this paper finds in PKs. Declared isomorphism of game structure; the theorem's origin is Nash/Kakutani, not football.
layer2.telemetry: Internal charting of directional call frequencies and per-direction success (first-down/stop outcomes) across games; partition-level Pearson correlations with bootstrap significance, mirroring the paper's subset test. No sportsbook inputs.

primitives.name: Statistical game against Nature: argmax selection inflates observed location-conditional conversion rates
primitives.verbatim_quote: However, we are not interested in the overall conversion-rates for these shot-locations but the simulated location-dependent conversion-rate when the 𝑃𝑃𝑃𝑃 is actually shot to that location (i.e., when that location has the higher expected value such that it is the revealed or optimal shot location). The former rates are never observed, whereas the latter are.
primitives.latex: \pi_{T,i}(C) \sim N(\mu=0.8,\,\sigma=0.05), \quad \pi_{T,i}(Z) \sim N(\mu=0.75,\,\sigma=0.05) \text{ independent}; \qquad s_i = \arg\max_{s\in\{C,Z\}} \pi_{T,i}(s); \qquad E[\pi_{T,i}(Z)\mid Z \text{ chosen}] = 0.814,\; E[\pi_{T,i}(C)\mid C \text{ chosen}] = 0.796
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: pi_{T,i}(s) = match-i expected conversion rate for location s, dimensionless probability; C = Center, Z = Corner; mu = distribution mean (0.8 Center, 0.75 Corner), probability units; sigma = 0.05 as written in the source (printed p.5, notation N(mu, sigma), not sigma-squared); i = match index; s_i = chosen location; the conditional expectations 0.814 / 0.796 are simulation estimates over 1e9 trials (dimensionless probabilities); P(Z chosen) = 0.76, P(C chosen) = 0.24 (printed p.5). Unconditional means remain 0.80000002 / 0.7500023 in the simulation (printed p.5).
primitives.assumptions: Nature draws the two location-conditional payoffs independently per match (independence justified by different physical demands: corner = pinpoint accuracy; center = fast approach, firm plant, pace; printed p.5); taker has rational expectations (Muth/Lucas-Prescott/Sargent lineage, printed p.5) - informed unbiased estimates before the kick; taker selects and executes the highest expected-payoff location; only chosen-location outcomes are observed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Selection bias is the point: observed conditional rates (0.814/0.796) exceed the unconditional draws (0.8/0.75) because only trials where a location is optimal are observed there - the former rates are never observed (printed p.6). If the taker cannot infer the draws (bounded rationality), or draws are correlated across locations, or execution noise is location-dependent, the argmax model and its +0.729 volume-rate correlation (printed p.7) fail. The 1e9-trial correlation is a property of the simulated game, not a sampling estimate from real kicks.

layer2.mapping: Any GSE evaluation of 'what works' that conditions on the chosen action inherits this selection kernel: deep-ball accuracy measured only on attempted deep balls, or fourth-down conversion measured only on attempted fourth downs, is E[pi_s | s chosen], not E[pi_s]. The kernel corrects the naive read: high observed success at high-volume locations can be pure argmax selection (positive correlation under optimization), so a positive volume-success correlation is NOT evidence of bias - only a negative one falsifies the optimizer null. Derived by instantiating the paper's statistical game on charted attempt/outcome pairs.
layer2.telemetry: Charted (available options, chosen action, outcome) triples from internal film/tracking data; estimate selection-corrected rates by modeling the choice rule; compare observed conditional rates to the argmax prediction. Internal data only.

primitives.name: Intersection-of-complements falsification design: H0 non-negative volume-conversion correlation across all partition subsets
primitives.verbatim_quote: Under msNe, we expect no correlation between volume and conversion-rate for any subset of the partitions. Under the statistical game equilibrium, we expect a positive correlation for all subsets of 8 the partitions. The intersection of the complement for these theoretical findings (i.e., that which we do not expect) is a negative correlation for some partition subset.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: rho_s = Pearson correlation between location-conditional shot-volume and location-conditional conversion-rate within partition subset s, dimensionless in [-1,1]; s = subset of the 8 goal-face partitions; the two model predictions are rho = 0 (msNe) and rho = +0.729 (statistical game, 200 resampled simulation pairs, printed p.7); empirical rejections: subset A (four corners) r = -0.749, bootstrap t = -7.71; subset B (four middles) r = -0.997, t = -10.85 (printed p.9); partition-level n = 8, shot-level n = 536.
primitives.assumptions: Both equilibrium models are treated as null hypotheses whose complements intersect in 'negative correlation for some subset'; bootstrap resampling (30 resamples per correlation, t-test of the sampling-distribution mean at alpha = 0.001) substitutes for large-sample inference because partition-level n = 8 (printed p.9); standard error of r taken as sqrt((1-r^2)/(n-2)) (printed p.9).
primitives.breakdown_regime: With 8 partitions, raw correlation significance is noisy - the bootstrap is load-bearing, and 30 resamples is a small resample count. The test rejects global equilibrium but cannot by itself identify the behavioral mechanism (optics vs risk aversion vs payoff misspecification); that requires the shot-level regressions. Aggregation across heterogeneous shooters can manufacture subset correlations (Simpson-type risk) - the paper subsets top/bottom precisely to control the risk geometry.

layer2.mapping: A falsification gate for any GSE optimizer claim: if the engine asserts agents optimize, then across every meaningful subset of the action space, volume-success correlation must be non-negative (zero under minimax mixing, positive under selection). A significantly negative subset correlation is a declared behavioral/misspecification alarm, exactly as the paper's -0.749/-0.997 reject both PK equilibria. The isomorphism is the hypothesis structure, transposed from goal partitions to play-type partitions.
layer2.telemetry: Internal play-type partitions (e.g., run/pass by field zone, fourth-down go/kick); bootstrap subset correlations of volume vs internal success metrics; log any negative subset as an optimizer-falsification event for review. No odds.

primitives.name: Revealed-preference regression and indifference-curve tradeoff: optimization utility priced 3.12x behavioral (optics) utility
primitives.verbatim_quote: The representative shooter would trade or give up a percentage point of conversion rate to raise his or her on-target rate by 3.12 percentage points with indifference according to Model 1. Conversely, the representative shooter would trade or give up a percentage point of on-target rate to increase his or her conversion rate by 0.32 percentage points with indifference according to Model 1. In other words, optimization utility is estimated to be 3.12 times as important to the representative PK-taker on the margin as is behavioral utility.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: y_i = a priori likelihood shot i is located to the revealed bin, dimensionless probability (linear-model fitted value, can exit [0,1]); x_{1,i} = expected conversion rate at revealed bin, leave-one-out over other shots to that bin (rational-expectations information set excludes the observed shot to avoid endogeneity, printed p.10), dimensionless probability; x_{2,i} = expected off-target rate given not-converted at revealed bin (behavioral variable: manner of failure has zero match-score effect, printed p.10), dimensionless probability; coefficients 1.492 and -0.477 are probability-per-probability, dimensionless; intercept -0.794 dimensionless. MRS = 1.492/0.477 = 3.128 (paper reports 3.12): percentage points of on-target rate given up per percentage point of conversion rate gained, dimensionless ratio. Lasso robustness: coefficients 1.154 (SE 0.024) and -0.387 (SE 0.007), best-fit MSE 0.0022 (printed p.11); R^2 85.2-86.8% (printed p.11).
primitives.assumptions: Representative shooter with a priori rational expectations formed from all OTHER shots to the bin (leave-one-out); linear specification (Model 1) and quadratic (Model 2, joint F-test preferred, printed p.11); behavioral variable is the manner-of-failure proportion (missed vs saved), which does not affect match score; Lasso with glmnet/selectiveInference for multicollinearity robustness (printed p.11).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Linear probability model: fitted y can leave [0,1]; the indifference-curve family is a local linear approximation, valid only within the observed (x1, x2) range. Risk aversion appears as the attenuating quadratic term (volume increases at a decreasing rate in conversion rate, printed p.11) - the linear MRS understates curvature at extremes. Leave-one-out expectations assume the shooter's information set matches the data partition; heterogeneous shooters or evolving keeper behavior break the representative-agent reading. n = 536 shots, 2015-2020 UEFA club competitions only.

layer2.mapping: Coach utility is not pure win-probability: it carries an optics term (manner of failure - missed FG vs blocked punt, turnover vs sack - all score-equivalent but reputationally distinct). The kernel estimates the revealed marginal rate of substitution between optimization and optics from decision data, with the paper's 3.12x ratio as the structural template: a GSE recommendation engine that ignores the optics budget will be systematically overridden by human operators, and the override is predictable, not irrational noise. Derived by transposing the leave-one-out revealed-preference design to fourth-down and special-teams decisions.
layer2.telemetry: Charted decisions with (expected success at chosen option, manner-of-failure profile of that option) from internal data; fit the two-variable revealed-preference model; report the MRS and its bootstrap interval; flag recommendations whose optics cost exceeds the operator's revealed budget.

primitives.name: Risk geometry of the goal face: border length, ground-as-bumper, and the miss/save asymmetry between top and bottom partitions
primitives.verbatim_quote: Each top partition is unequivocally riskier than its southern neighbor in the bottom-half of the goal. For example, top corner partitions each have 10 feet of post-or-crossbar borders versus 4 feet for bottom-corner partitions. Top-middle partitions each have 6 feet of post-or-crossbar borders versus 0 feet for bottom-middle partitions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: A_partition = area of one goal-face partition, ft^2 (24); total goal face 8 ft x 24 ft = 192 ft^2 (printed p.2); L_border = length of post-or-crossbar border exposed to a partition, feet (top corner 10, bottom corner 4, top middle 6, bottom middle 0; printed p.8); empirical outcome rates: top-partition miss-goal rate 12.88% vs bottom 2.48%; top save rate 5.30% vs bottom 23.51% (printed p.9), dimensionless percentages over n = 536 shots; off-target shots pinned to the Euclidean-nearest partition as intended target (printed p.2).
primitives.assumptions: 8 equal-area partitions of the goal face (Almeida et al. 2016 scheme, printed p.2); professional shooters assumed sufficiently skilled to always shoot to or nearest their intended partition; the ground acts as a guidance mechanism ('bumpers in bowling') steering off-target bottom shots toward target, with no analogous mechanism for top shots (printed p.8); top shots additionally require simultaneous lift and placement (printed p.8).
primitives.breakdown_regime: The nearest-partition pinning of off-target shots is an intent assumption, not an observation - it can misattribute wide misses. Border-length risk is geometric, but actual miss probabilities also depend on shooter-specific lift/placement skill, fatigue, and weather (the paper's Nature draws); the 12.88%/2.48% split is a 2015-2020 UEFA club-competition estimate, not a universal constant. Partition-level inference with n = 8 requires the bootstrap machinery of p3.

layer2.mapping: Every high-leverage target in the 22-player system has a border geometry: a deep sideline route has more 'out-of-bounds border' than a middle-of-field seam; a tight-window throw has more interception border than a checkdown. The miss/save asymmetry transposes to turnover/incomplete asymmetry: failures differ in manner even when score-equivalent, and the ground-as-bumper effect maps to margin-of-error structures (sideline vs hash, pocket vs scramble). The isomorphism is between partitioned risk geometries with outcome-manner asymmetry, not a claim that soccer physics governs football.
layer2.telemetry: Internal charting of target zones with border exposure (sideline proximity, window tightness) and failure-manner decomposition (missed vs saved / incomplete vs turnover); compare zone-conditional volume against the risk geometry to detect optics-driven underuse of high-border zones.

reasoning_traces.think:
The paper's first sovereign object is a null model, not a description. The classical PK game (7f0f084cdb020856:p1, printed p.2-4) is constant-sum: the taker wants to avoid coordinating on location, the goalkeeper wants to coordinate. Table 1's best-response arrows show no pure equilibrium, so Nash's existence theorem (via Kakutani's fixed point, cited printed p.3) guarantees a mixed one. The indifference conditions - Eq. (3) 0.7 p_t + 0.1(1-p_t) = 0.1 p_t + 0.3(1-p_t) giving p_t* = 1/4, and Eq. (4) giving q_G* = 1/4 - are not fitting devices; they are the definition of equilibrium as mutual marginal indifference. The deep consequence is the zero-correlation prediction (printed p.4-5): at msNe, location-conditional shot-volume carries no information about location-conditional conversion-rate, because any emerging return differential is anticipated and countered until returns equalize at pi_T* = 3/4. This is the same logic as Shannon's capacity-achieving matching: strategic interaction drives the observable signature of advantage to zero.

The second model (p2, printed p.5-6) replaces the strategic goalkeeper with Nature: independent normal draws of location-conditional conversion rates, N(0.8, 0.05) for Center and N(0.75, 0.05) for Corner, a taker with rational expectations who selects the argmax. Here the signature flips: because only chosen locations are observed, the observed conditional rates are selection-inflated (0.814 Corner, 0.796 Center versus unconditional 0.8/0.75), and volume correlates positively with conversion rate (+0.729 over 200 resampled simulation pairs, printed p.7). The selection kernel is the load-bearing insight: E[pi_s | s chosen] is not E[pi_s], and the direction of the bias is toward the chosen location looking better than it is.

The falsification design (p3, printed p.7-8) is the methodological crown: neither model alone is testable against the other, but the intersection of their complements is sharp. msNe predicts rho = 0 everywhere; the statistical game predicts rho > 0 everywhere; therefore any optimizing behavior consistent with either model implies H0: rho_s >= 0 for every partition subset s. A significantly negative subset correlation falsifies the entire optimizer class at once. The data deliver exactly that: corners r = -0.749 (bootstrap t = -7.71), middles r = -0.997 (t = -10.85), printed p.9. The top/bottom subsetting is not arbitrary - it is dictated by the risk geometry (p5): top partitions carry 10 feet of border versus 4 for bottom corners, miss-goal rates 12.88% versus 2.48%, save rates 5.30% versus 23.51%. High shots fail by missing; low shots fail by being saved. The manner of failure is score-irrelevant but reputationally loaded, which is where the behavioral term enters.

For the GSE engine the lesson is structural: equilibrium is a null hypothesis with a testable signature, not an assumption to be imposed. When charted play-calling shows negative volume-success correlation within a partition subset, the correct inference is a behavioral or misspecification alarm - the same alarm this paper rings for elite PK takers - and the correct response is to estimate the revealed utility (p4) rather than to lecture the operator about expected value. The cross-layer chain runs game theory -> selection statistics -> falsification design -> revealed preference, and each layer constrains the next.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The hidden state behind this paper is a century-old scar in economics: the assumption that agents maximize, repeatedly embarrassed by evidence. The paper's own lineage cites Nash (1950) and Kakutani (1941) for equilibrium existence, Osborne and Rubinstein (1994) for the definition, and Muth (1961), Lucas-Prescott (1981), Sargent (1972) for rational expectations (printed p.3, 5, references p.15). The behavioral counter-lineage is Romer (2006) on NFL fourth-down conservatism and Goff-Locke (2019) showing it is not fully explained by risk aversion, plus the Shaq/Drummond underhand-free-throw optics anecdote (printed p.1-2). The paper's contribution is to fuse the two lineages into a single falsifiable null - non-negative correlation - rather than treating optimization and behavior as rival religions. No origin is claimed in football; the NFL citations are empirical precedents, not the source of the mathematics.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Three minds collide at the penalty spot. The taker models the keeper's dive tendency and wants to be unpredictable; the keeper models the taker's habits and wants to coordinate; both know the other is modeling. At msNe this recursion terminates in indifference - neither can gain by unilateral deviation - but the paper's data show the recursion does not terminate there in reality, because a third audience enters: the crowd, the media, the coach's future self. The taker is not playing only the keeper; he is playing the observer who will judge a miss-the-goal failure as incompetent and a saved failure as unlucky. The keeper, symmetrically, dives to be seen diving. Theory of mind under pressure is therefore multi-audience: the strategic opponent is the least of the taker's problems, because the optics audience never randomizes and never forgives.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The cross-layer veto runs from statistics to psychology to the engine. Suppose the GSE optimizer recommends a high-volume shift toward the highest-conversion action partition. The selection kernel (p2) warns that the observed advantage may be argmax inflation, and the falsification gate (p3) warns that if any subset already shows negative volume-success correlation, the optimizer null is falsified for this agent population - pushing volume harder will not converge to equilibrium, it will amplify the behavioral deviation. The psychological layer supplies the mechanism: the optics budget (p4) means operators will override pure-EV advice at a revealed rate of roughly three-to-one against optics-costly options. The adjudication: veto any recommendation that assumes away the optics term; re-price it with the revealed MRS before queueing. A recommendation that is mathematically optimal but predictably overridden is operationally worthless.

reasoning_traces.think:
The second cluster of invariants concerns measurement of preferences from behavior. The regression design (7f0f084cdb020856:p4, printed p.9-11) is careful about endogeneity: the shooter's rational expectation of a bin's conversion rate is formed from all OTHER shots to that bin, leaving the observed shot out of the information set. The dependent variable is the a priori likelihood of locating to the revealed bin, likewise formed from other shots. This leave-one-out construction is what licenses a causal reading of the coefficients rather than a mechanical correlation: the shooter is modeled as responding to an expectation that does not contain his own response.

The fitted Model 1 (Eq. 7, printed p.12) is y = -0.794 + 1.492 x1 - 0.477 x2, where x1 is expected conversion rate (the optimization variable, score-relevant) and x2 is expected off-target rate given not-converted (the behavioral variable, score-irrelevant: a miss and a save both produce zero goals, printed p.10). Both coefficients are highly significant; R^2 spans 85.2-86.8% across specifications; the Lasso robustness check returns 1.154 (SE 0.024) and -0.387 (SE 0.007) with best-fit MSE 0.0022 (printed p.11), so multicollinearity does not explain the behavioral term away. The quadratic Model 2, preferred by joint F-test, shows volume increasing at a decreasing rate in conversion rate - risk aversion on top of the optics preference, echoing Romer's NFL fourth-down findings (printed p.11, 14).

The indifference-curve construction (printed p.12-13) converts the regression into economics: fix y = y0 and solve for the (x1, on-target-rate) tradeoff line. The slope ratio 1.492/0.477 = 3.12 is the revealed marginal rate of substitution: the representative shooter gives up one percentage point of conversion rate to gain 3.12 percentage points of on-target rate. Optimization utility is priced 3.12 times behavioral utility at the margin - not infinitely more, which is the pure-optimizer fantasy, and not comparably, which would be pure optics. The number is a budget, and budgets can be spent.

The risk geometry (p5, printed p.8-9) explains why the optics term has the sign it does: top partitions expose 10 feet of border versus 4 for bottom corners, and the ground steers low misses toward target like bowling bumpers. Missing the goal entirely is the signature failure of aiming high; being saved is the signature failure of aiming low. Since the manner of failure is score-irrelevant, any preference over it is revealed behavioral utility, full stop. The paper's conclusion - hybrid decision-makers, part rational optimizers part appearance-keepers (printed p.14) - is the honest synthesis, and it generalizes: every high-leverage decision in the 22-player system carries a manner-of-failure profile that operators price, whether or not the engine models it. For DFS portfolio construction the same discipline applies internally: lineup exposure choices reveal a risk/optics budget too, and tail-risk management must respect the revealed budget rather than assume variance-neutrality - all without any sportsbook odds input.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The revealed-preference machinery descends from Samuelson's program of reading utility off choice rather than introspection, and the rational-expectations information-set construction descends from Muth (1961) through Lucas-Prescott (1981) and Sargent (1972), all cited in the paper (printed p.5, references p.15). The leave-one-out expectation device is an econometric answer to a specific scar: simultaneity bias - the shooter's choice contaminates any expectation formed from a sample that includes that choice. The Lasso robustness layer descends from the machine-learning regularization literature (glmnet, selectiveInference, printed p.11), a response to the multicollinearity scar in small-n sports samples. The indifference-curve rendering is standard microeconomic geometry transposed onto a regression plane; the paper's novelty is applying the whole stack to the manner-of-failure variable, which is score-neutral by construction.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The shooter's theory of mind now includes himself as an object: he knows that observers will read a wide miss as a choke, so he aims lower than conversion-maximization dictates, and he knows the keeper knows this, which partially restores the value of low shots. The coach's theory of mind is recursive in the other direction: he must decide whether to correct the shooter's optics bias or exploit it - a shooter who reliably aims low is predictable to a keeper who charts him. The engine's theory of mind must model both: the operator's revealed MRS (3.12x in this sample) predicts which recommendations will be overridden, and the opponent's charting predicts which behavioral regularities will be punished. Under pressure, the recursive chain does not converge to indifference because the optics audience's payoffs never mix - they are fixed, social, and unforgiving.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The veto here is against the engine's own purity. A recommendation system that maximizes expected goals alone will propose high-border targets (top corners, deep sideline shots) whenever their conversion expectation dominates. The revealed-preference layer vetoes this in two stages: first, the operator's optics budget means such recommendations are overridden at a predictable rate, so queueing them wastes decision capital; second, the risk-aversion curvature (Model 2) means the operator's marginal valuation of conversion itself attenuates at high rates, so the pure-EV ranking is wrong even on the optimization axis. The physiological layer adds that lift-plus-placement demands (printed p.8) raise execution variance under fatigue, widening the effective border late in games. The adjudication: re-price every high-border recommendation with the revealed MRS and the fatigue-adjusted execution variance before it reaches the queue; a veto is not a failure of the engine but the engine modeling its operator correctly.

universal_lens: Audit lens: separate the null model from the description. Equilibrium predictions are testable signatures (zero or positive volume-success correlation), and a single significantly negative subset correlation falsifies the whole optimizer class. Never read a conditional-on-choice success rate as an unconditional rate: argmax selection inflates it. And never assume the manner of failure is neutral - score-equivalent outcomes carry revealed behavioral prices.
gsi_mapping: GSI lens: the selection kernel E[pi_s | s chosen] != E[pi_s] is the same bias that inflates clinical outcome statistics conditioned on treatment choice - patients selected for a procedure are not random draws, so observed success overstates the procedure's unconditional effect. The rational-expectations information-set construction maps to how clinicians form prognoses from prior cases (leave-one-out avoids self-contamination), and the optics budget maps to defensive medicine: score-irrelevant manner-of-failure preferences (litigation optics) measurably shift choice away from outcome-optimal actions, a testable revealed-preference hypothesis for clinical telemetry.
gse_mapping: GSE lens: Coach-Mind consumes p1's indifference null, p2's selection-corrected evaluation kernel, p3's subset-correlation falsification gate, and p4's revealed MRS as an operator model: recommendations are re-priced against the optics budget before queueing, and negative subset correlations raise behavioral alarms. DFS portfolio tail risk respects revealed risk budgets internally, never via sportsbook odds. All artifacts remain internal; nothing is published, sent, or deployed.
